newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay court rules army rebel cannot be cleared.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay court rules army rebel cannot be cleared.

text.p: The Paraguayan Supreme Court on Friday threw out an appeals court ruling that cleared army rebel Lino Oviedo of attempted rebellion, and ruled that the former general's trial must continue.

Legal officials said the country's highest court had decided that the January ruling that cleared Oviedo of attempted rebellion against the government of President Juan Carlos Wasmosy was "completely arbitrary and illegal."
In April 1996, Oviedo, a populist cavalry officer in charge of the army, holed himself up in his barracks with his men resisting a discharge order by Wasmosy.
The standoff caused fears of a military coup, but ended in peace after Wasmosy first offered Oviedo the defence ministry, then stripped him of his rank and put him in jail.

Oviedo, head of a splinter faction of the ruling Colorado Party who wants to run for president next year, denied he tried to overthrow Wasmosy and the appeals court ruled that he did eventually follow the president's orders and step down.

One recent opinion poll suggested Oviedo could make an impact in the May 1998 presidential, congressional and regional elections. It said he had 40 percent support among Colorado voters and was their favourite choice to run for president.

Oviedo was instrumental in the 1989 coup that ended the dictatorship of Gen. Alfredo Stroessner and helped Wasmosy win the presidency in 1993 elections. But he now accuses Wasmosy of corruption and alleges that the president urged him to attempt a coup that would shut down Congress last April.
